commitResults.messageTitle: Save meetings to and load them from the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
Meetings exist in the model but are not written to addressbook.json,
so any meetings added are lost when PingBook closes.

Add JsonAdaptedMeeting to convert meetings to and from JSON, storing
the date and times in the same DD/MM/YYYY and HHMM formats users type
so the file stays human-editable. JsonSerializableAddressBook now
saves the meeting list and loads it back, rejecting invalid fields
and duplicate meetings the same way it does for persons.

Data files from before this change have no "meetings" key; these are
treated as having no meetings, so existing data still loads.

Make MeetingName's name field public so JsonAdaptedMeeting can read
it, matching how JsonAdaptedPerson reads Name's public fullName.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename client commands to addc, deletec and listc
commitResults.messageBody:
The add, delete and list commands use AB3's generic names. PingBook
will also manage meetings, with addm, deletem and listm, so the
generic names no longer make clear which list a command acts on.

Rename them to addc, deletec and listc.

LogicManagerTest hard-coded "delete 9", which would now fail as an
unknown command instead of testing the invalid-index error. Build it
from DeleteCommand.COMMAND_WORD so it follows future renames.
Update storage for meetings

JsonAdaptedMeeting and the meeting support in
JsonSerializableAddressBook have no tests, so a regression in how
meetings are saved or loaded would go unnoticed.

Add tests covering:

* converting a meeting to JSON and back
* rejecting each missing or invalid meeting field
* rejecting duplicate meetings, including ones differing only in
  name case
* loading older data files with no "meetings" key as an empty list
* saving meetings to a file and reading them back

Add a TypicalMeetings test utility, modelled on TypicalPersons, to
provide the sample meetings these tests share.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make address optional in addc command
commitResults.messageBody:
addc currently rejects any command without an a/ADDRESS parameter,
which contradicts the agreed spec where only name, phone and email
are compulsory.

Allow a client to be added without an address. An omitted address is
stored as an empty address, while an explicit but blank a/ is still
rejected, so users cannot accidentally clear the field. The usage
message now shows a/ADDRESS as optional.

Persisted data with an empty address is accepted when loading, so a
client added without an address survives a restart.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject meetings that end at or before their start
commitResults.messageBody:
Meetings are currently accepted with an end time earlier than or equal
to the start time, which describes no real time slot and would make any
overlap check meaningless.

Add Meeting#isValidTimeRange and reject such input in addm and editm
with a dedicated error message. editm checks the final merged times,
so changing only st or only et is covered as well.

commitResults.messageTitle: Block overlapping meetings unless force/ is given
commitResults.messageBody:
Nothing stops the user from scheduling two meetings at the same time,
even though the user guide lists a warning for clashes as a goal.

Treat two meetings as overlapping when they are on the same date and
their time ranges intersect; back-to-back meetings do not overlap.
addm and editm now fail with an error that lists the conflicting
meetings (at most three, then a count of the rest). Adding a valueless
force/ saves the meeting anyway and appends a warning to the success
message. editm ignores the meeting being edited, so changing a
meeting's own time never conflicts with itself.

Overlaps are computed on demand and not stored, so the JSON format is
unchanged and saved files that already contain overlaps still load.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add parser tests for the force/ prefix
commitResults.messageBody:
PR #128 added force/ to CliSyntax.getAllPrefixes() and made each
parser reject prefixes it does not support, but only addm and editm
have tests that exercise force/.

Add tests that addc, findc, findm, listc, listm, deletec and deletem
reject force/ with their usage message. Add editm tests for force/
placed before the fields, and for force/ given alone, which fails
with MESSAGE_NOT_EDITED. This shows the prefix is accepted and only
the missing edit field is the problem.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add dedicated editc test for force/ rejection
commitResults.messageBody:
EditClientCommandParserTest only covers force/ through a bare
"1 force/" line inside the invalid-preamble test. That input has no
fields to edit, so it could fail for a reason other than force/ being
an unsupported prefix. The test is also hard to find under that
heading.

Add a separate test that pairs force/ with a valid field. The
parser's prefix check is then the only reason it can be rejected.
Add parser tests for the force/ prefix

Master does not compile its tests. The force/ test added in #137 uses
the statically imported MESSAGE_INVALID_COMMAND_FORMAT, but #138
replaced that import with a Messages import when it was merged.

Qualify the constant as Messages.MESSAGE_INVALID_COMMAND_FORMAT, as the
other tests in the file already do.
Fix compile error in FindMeetingCommandParserTest

commitResults.messageTitle: Match findc keywords as substrings of names
commitResults.messageBody:
findc only matches whole words, so "Han" does not find "Hans Gruber",
while findm already matches keywords anywhere in a meeting name. The
two find commands behave inconsistently.

Make findc match a keyword if it appears anywhere in the person's name,
ignoring case. Keywords are still split on whitespace and combined with
OR, as in findm. Only names are searched, as before.

Update the User Guide to say that partial words match, and add
predicate tests for matches at the start, middle and end of a word.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check overlaps against all meetings, not the filtered list
commitResults.messageBody:
getOverlappingMeetings() searches the meetings currently on display.
When a listm filter is active, meetings hidden by the filter are not
checked, so addm and editm can save a double booking without force/
and without any overlap warning.

Search every stored meeting instead, sorted in the display order so
the overlap message still lists conflicts chronologically. The index
used to pick the meeting to edit still refers to the displayed list.

Add tests that reproduce the bug at the model level and through
EditMeetingCommand, with and without force/.
editm allows overlapping meetings when the conflicting meeting is hidden by a filter
